gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 7?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 7 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Official observations from the German Weather Service will resolve the market once final readings are confirmed. Unexpected shifts such as increased cloud cover, localized showers, or revisions in the final model runs could still alter the measured maximum.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency project a maximum of 35°C for Tokyo on August 8 under partly cloudy skies, yet trader consensus clusters tightly around 33–34°C amid model spreads in sea-breeze timing and afternoon cloud development that can shave 1–2°C from peak readings. High humidity near 70–80% and the urban heat island effect amplify apparent temperatures, but variable wind patterns and any earlier marine layer intrusion often cap actual maxima below guidance. Historical August baselines average 30–32°C, so the narrow 33–34°C band reflects ongoing uncertainty in short-term convective inhibition and observational updates before the daily close.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Japan Meteorological Agency guidance and ensemble model runs for August 9 point to a partly cloudy day with ample afternoon insolation, supporting peak temperatures near the seasonal average of 31–32 °C while allowing modest exceedance under sustained clear conditions. The tight spread between the 32 °C and 33 °C contracts captures uncertainty in cloud timing, boundary-layer mixing, and the urban heat-island enhancement typical of central Tokyo stations. Light steering winds and high humidity limit rapid intensification, yet any delay in afternoon convection could add 1 °C; conversely, scattered showers would cap readings near 32 °C. Traders are therefore weighting the most probable narrow range consistent with official forecast thresholds and historical August variability.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Latest National Weather Service guidance and ensemble model runs position mid-90s as the most likely outcome for Central Park’s August 9 high, reflecting a warm, humid air mass advected northward by the Bermuda High.** Persistent southwesterly flow has kept recent NYC highs near or above 88–90 °F, with dew points in the mid-70s supporting heat indices well into the 90s despite modest cloud cover or scattered convection. The Climate Prediction Center’s August outlook favors above-normal temperatures across the Northeast, consistent with the current 90-plus pattern through the first half of the month. Primary uncertainty stems from the timing and coverage of afternoon thunderstorms, which could cap the high a degree or two lower if they develop earlier than modeled; conversely, clearer skies would favor the upper end of the 92–93 °F bin that currently carries the highest market-implied probability. Updated NWS point forecasts and 12Z model guidance expected later today will be the next key inputs for traders.

eventMetadata.context_description: Current Japan Meteorological Agency forecasts and ensemble model runs for Tokyo on August 8 project a daily maximum near 34°C, driven by persistent summer high pressure, light winds, and typical seasonal insolation under mostly clear to partly cloudy skies. This aligns with 2026's above-normal temperature outlook across central Japan, where urban heat island effects and high humidity often push observed maxima toward the upper end of climatological ranges (30–35°C). Traders assign overwhelming probability to 34°C because real-time observations and short-range guidance show little deviation from this value. Unanticipated afternoon convection, stronger on-shore flow, or a localized measurement anomaly at the official station could still shift the recorded high into the 33°C or 35°C bin.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Official Japan Meteorological Agency guidance currently projects a mostly cloudy day on August 9 with a daytime maximum near 35°C, yet trader consensus clusters tightly around 32–33°C.** This split reflects model spread in how much afternoon insolation will be reduced by increasing cloud cover and the risk of late-day showers. 

Key variables include the strength and timing of any frontal moisture arriving from the south, boundary-layer humidity that limits surface heating despite subtropical high pressure, and Tokyo’s urban heat island effect, which can add 1–2°C relative to surrounding rural stations depending on wind speed. Historical mid-August climatology for the Kanto plain shows typical peaks of 31–34°C under similar regimes, with occasional 35°C+ when skies remain clearer longer. 

Resolution hinges on the official JMA Tokyo observation; any earlier cloud build-up or brief shower could cap the high at 32–33°C, while sustained sunshine would support the higher end of guidance. Updated model runs and the evening JMA briefing will likely narrow the range further.

**High pressure dominating southern England and a warming trend under sunny conditions position 31–32°C as the most likely daily maximum for London on August 9.** Official Met Office guidance currently forecasts a peak of 32°C, supported by ensemble model consensus showing light winds, minimal cloud cover, and advection of warmer air masses that favor temperatures climbing from recent values near 28°C on August 8.  

Climatologically, early-August London maxima average around 22–24°C, so the current setup represents a notable positive anomaly driven by persistent anticyclonic conditions rather than transient factors. Trader consensus, reflected in the 44% implied probability for 31°C and 29.5% for 32°C, aggregates live observational feeds and short-range model runs, with narrower spreads around 30°C or 33°C accounting for possible urban heat-island effects at key stations or minor forecast revisions.  

No major model disagreements have emerged in the latest updates, though final resolution will hinge on the precise timing of peak heating and any localized convective development before the close of the meteorological day.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 10 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the London City Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/gb/london/EGLC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest Met Office guidance points to a 27°C peak for London on August 10 under building high pressure, yet the tight clustering of market-implied odds around 26–28°C reflects substantial ensemble spread in short-range models. Diurnal heating under mostly clear skies could push readings to 27–28°C if boundary-layer mixing remains limited, while modest Atlantic moisture or increased cloud could cap the maximum near 25–26°C. Historical August maxima in central London average near 23°C, so the current warm anomaly stems from a persistent subtropical ridge, though small steering errors in the jet stream can shift outcomes by 2–3°C. Updated ECMWF and Met Office runs expected within 24 hours will likely narrow the range before settlement.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service and AccuWeather model runs position a high of 90–91°F as the most likely outcome for New York City on August 8, aligning with the 56% market-implied probability. Persistent Bermuda High influence, combined with moderate southerly flow and dew points in the mid-70s, supports daytime maxima near or slightly above the 83°F August climatological average from Central Park observations. Ensemble guidance shows limited spread, with only modest afternoon mixing or cloud cover potentially capping readings at 92–93°F (29% odds) or holding them to 88–89°F (13.5%). Warmer-than-normal seasonal signals from the Climate Prediction Center reinforce trader focus on this narrow range, with final verification depending on official LaGuardia Airport observations.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest ensemble forecasts from the DWD and ECMWF place Munich’s August 10 maximum most likely near 33–34 °C, driven by continued high-pressure ridging and warm southeasterly advection under largely clear skies. Subtle model spread in boundary-layer mixing depth, timing of any weak frontal passage, and afternoon convective inhibition accounts for the close 38.5 % versus 31.5 % implied probabilities on 34 °C and 33 °C. Historical August climatology shows daily highs averaging 23–25 °C, so current guidance reflects a modest heat anomaly; any increase in low-level moisture or earlier cloud build-up could shave 1–2 °C off the peak, while stronger insolation would support the 35 °C tail. Updated model runs and DWD briefings over the next 48 hours remain the key data points traders are monitoring.

Seasonal norms for Munich in early August are 23–25 °C, so this episode represents a clear positive anomaly driven by subsidence and clear conditions.

The 35 °C bucket (17.5 %) captures tail risk if insolation proves stronger than modeled or if downslope warming is enhanced. Lower outcomes remain unlikely given the consensus for continued high pressure and minimal precipitation. Updated model cycles and any shifts in observed 2-m temperatures or 850 hPa thickness over the next 24 hours will determine whether the market tilts decisively toward 33 °C or 34 °C at resolution.

Seasonal norms for Munich in early August are 23–25 °C, so this episode represents a clear positive anomaly driven by subsidence and clear conditions.

The 35 °C bucket (17.5 %) captures tail risk if insolation proves stronger than modeled or if downslope warming is enhanced. Lower outcomes remain unlikely given the consensus for continued high pressure and minimal precipitation. Updated model cycles and any shifts in observed 2-m temperatures or 850 hPa thickness over the next 24 hours will determine whether the market tilts decisively toward 33 °C or 34 °C at resolution.
